results:
The sources agree that Pelayo's rebellion began against the Berber governor Munuza, but they differ on the trigger and the date.

- **Election and revolt:** The Crónica Albeldense says Asturian nobles chose Pelayo as caudillo in an assembly, and he then led the uprising against Munuza, who was based near Gijón (Pelayo fue elegido caudillo en asamblea por los nobles astures y, como tal, lideró la rebelión contra el poder del bereber Munuza, establecido cerca de Gijón.).
- **Trigger, marriage or tax:** The Crónica Rotense blames Munuza's courtship of Pelayo's sister, which led to Pelayo's return to Asturias around 717 (Munuza, afincado en Gijón, envió a Pelayo a Córdoba con el pretexto de una comisión, para, en su ausencia, desposarse con su hermana. Este hecho provocó el regreso de Pelayo a Asturias en el verano de 717.). A Spanish article from the Fundación Disenso argues that the main driver was instead the doubling of the tribute demanded by the valí Anbasa in 721 (todo parece indicar que el principal detonante de la revuelta pelagiana fue la duplicación del tributo).
- **Date:** Muy Interesante places the start of his caudillaje and rebellion in 718 (Los historiadores sitúan el comienzo efectivo del caudillaje de Pelayo y el estallido de su rebelión en el año 718.).
- **Britannica:** It describes him leading a revolt of Asturians and Visigothic refugees against Munuza, then being captured and sent to Córdoba before escaping in 717 and resuming the rebellion (He survived the defeat (711) of the Visigoths by the Moors at the Battle of Guadalete near Medina Sidonia and reached his native Asturias, where he led a revolt of Asturians and Visigothic refugees against the Moorish governor Munuza. He was captured and sent to Córdoba as a hostage but escaped (717) and again assumed leadership of the Asturian rebellion.).

Overall, the sources do not give a single "first action." The most consistent account is the Albeldense's: election by the nobles, then revolt against Munuza. The tax-increase explanation is the main alternative to the sister/marriage story, and the 717 and 718 dates are not fully reconciled. The Covadonga battle in 722 came later.

content.text:
**答案：** 佩拉约（Pelayo）被阿斯图里亚斯贵族推举为首领（caudillo）后，做的第一件大事是起兵反抗驻在希洪的柏柏尔总督穆努萨（Munuza），也就是拒绝再向穆斯林当局纳贡、公开造反。来源一般把这件事放在 718 年前后。这场起事后来在 722 年打成了科瓦东加战役（Batalla de Covadonga）。

起义的导火索，几处来源说法不一样。《罗托编年史》（Crónica Rotense）说是穆努萨想娶佩拉约的妹妹。也有观点认为是因为 721 年总督 Anbasa 把贡赋翻了一倍。

（搜了 1 次。）

依据：
- [Muy Interesante](https://muyinteresante.okdiario.com/historia/34975.html)
- [Fundación Disenso – Covadonga](https://fundaciondisenso.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/20230124_Covadonga.pdf)
- [Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/print/article/449116)
- [El Debate – Batalla de Covadonga](https://www.eldebate.com/historia/20250528/batalla-covadonga-convirtio-don-pelayo-primer-heroe-reconquista_301497_amp.html)
